newsitem.title: UK: First public performance at Shakespeare Globe.
newsitem.headline: First public performance at Shakespeare Globe.

text.p: Theatregoers stepped backed into the 16th century on Tuesday when Britain's Globe Theatre, an exquisite reconstruction of William Shakespeare's Elizabethan playhouse, staged its first public performance.

Up to 1,500 people crowded into the open-air wooden theatre for the performance. Just as Shakespeare's contemporaries had done, they stood, saundered or sat on wooden benches and hissed and booed at the appropriate moments.

The 30 million pound ($50 million) project on the south side of the River Thames opposite St Paul's Cathedral -- on the site of the original Globe theatre -- was the brainchild of the late U.S. director Paul Wanamaker.
Ten years in the making and meticulously constructed, it is expected to be completed by September 1999, the 400th anniversary of the first recorded performance at the Globe.

Artistic director Mark Rylance, who took the title role, made sure every aspect of Tuesday's performance of Henry V was as authentic as possible with an all-male cast performing all the roles as they would have done in Shakespeare's day.
The costumes were made using Elizabethan sewing techinques and some of the audience, who stood in front of the stage, paid only a penny as they would have 400 years ago.

"In my indulgent romantic moments, in my hand-stitched costumes, I do feel the shadow of the past but this is no theme park or museum theatre," actor David Fielder said at the official opening last week.
